title: US Foods Rebound From Pandemic Years Continues to Reward Investors
content:
Quick Read

A $1,000 investment in the US Foods (USFD) initial public offering a decade ago would be worth almost $3,700 today. The stock has surged particularly since being crushed by the pandemic, and the bull case now looks reasonable. The analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 stocks and US Foods wasn't one of them. Get them here FREE.

From Blocked Merger to Independent Operator

US Foods (NYSE: USFD) hit public markets in May 2016 after the FTC blocked its proposed sale to Sysco the prior year. What started as a fallback plan turned into a decade of building. The Rosemont, Illinois-based distributor now serves roughly 250,000 customer locations through more than 70 broadline distribution centers and over 90 cash-and-carry stores, with about 30,000 associates handling roughly $39.4 billion in annual sales.

The story since the IPO has three chapters. First, steady share gains with independent restaurants. Second, a brutal pandemic shock that crushed restaurant volumes and the stock. Third, a sharp rebound under CEO Dave Flitman, anchored by the CHEF'STORE acquisition in 2020 and recent broadline tuck-ins like Jake's Finer Foods in Houston and Shetakis in Las Vegas. Management is now exploring a sale of the CHEF'STORE cash-and-carry business to focus on core distribution.

$1,000 Invested at IPO Is Now $3,690

In the following table, investment date assumes the first available trading price after IPO. The starting investment in US Foods in each period is $1,000.

The analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 stocks and US Foods wasn't one of them.Get them here FREE.

Time Period Total Return Ending Value S&P 500 Return 1 Year 34.3% $1,343.20 28.5% 3 Years 138.8% $2,388.40 75.5% 5 Years 129.1% $2,290.80 71.5% Since IPO (May 2016) 269.1% $3,690.50 245.8%

Roughly tripling your money over a decade is solid, and it outperforms the S&P 500's run over the same span. The shape of the journey matters: shares cratered in early 2020 as restaurants closed, and patient holders had to stomach years of choppy recovery. The real outperformance occurred over the past three years, as US Foods surged when margins finally inflected.

FY2025 cemented the turn: revenue of $39.42 billion (+4.08%), net income of $676 million (+36.84%), and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.98. The company pays no dividend but announced a fresh $1 billion buyback in November 2025.

The Bull Case, With One Eye on the Consumer

The bull case rests on Flitman delivering his 20% adjusted EPS CAGR through 2027, and it is straightforward: 19 consecutive quarters of independent restaurant growth, 2026 guidance calling for 18% to 24% adjusted EPS growth, and a forward P/E around 31 that looks reasonable for that trajectory.

Story Continues

The bear case hinges on whether consumer spending is weakening. Chain volume fell 3.4% in Q4, GLP-1 adoption is a real demand overhang, and $4.6 billion of debt limits flexibility in a downturn. Revenue has missed estimates in four of the past six quarters, even as EPS beats pile up.

The execution has been consistent, and the buyback provides a floor.

title: Is It Time To Reassess Sysco (SYY) After Recent Price Swings And DCF Outlook?

This article looks at key valuation metrics for Sysco at around US$73.97 so you can assess whether the current price appears reasonable or potentially attractive. Recent coverage of Sysco has focused on its role as a major foodservice distributor and its position within the broader consumer retailing space. This context helps frame whether the recent share price moves are consistent with how the business is being discussed in the market. Sysco currently has a valuation score of 4 out of 6. The following sections break down what that score reflects across different valuation methods and conclude with a broader perspective on how investors might think about what the stock could be worth.

Find out why Sysco's 6.6% return over the last year is lagging behind its peers.

Approach 1: Sysco Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Analysis

A Discounted Cash Flow model estimates what a business could be worth by projecting its future cash flows and then discounting those amounts back to today, using the time value of money.

For Sysco, the model used is a 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach, based on cash flow projections in US$. The latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $1.79b. Analyst inputs are used for the earlier years, then Simply Wall St extrapolates further out, with projected free cash flow of $3.51b in 2030. Across the ten year window, discounted projections range from roughly $2.30b in 2026 to $1.99b in 2035, reflecting how future cash is adjusted back to today’s terms.

When these discounted cash flows are added together, the model points to an estimated intrinsic value of $150.31 per share. Against the recent share price of about $73.97, the DCF output implies a 50.8% discount, which indicates that the stock appears materially undervalued on this measure.

title: Sysco Corporation: Dominating the Plate
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

SYSCO's Global Architecture of Food Distribution

Sysco Corporation is currently undergoing the most radical transformation in its 56-year history. Traditionally, Sysco has been defined by its "moat" of route density and logistical scale, a high-touch, delivery-centric system that serves 730,000 customer locations across 10 countries. However, the March 30, 2026, announcement of a $29.1 billion acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot signals a pivot away from pure-play delivery toward a hybrid "multi-channel" architecture.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with SYY. Is SYY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

While Sysco's legacy advantage lies in the efficiency of its 337 distribution centers and its ability to handle "white glove" service for high-volume accounts, the Jetro acquisition attempts to capture a fundamentally different segment: the "fill-in" and price-sensitive small independent operator. The market's immediate 1316% sell-off of SYY stock reflects a deep-seated skepticism regarding this combination. Investors are grappling with whether a management team optimized for route-density and delivery-logistics can successfully govern a high-turnover, low-service warehouse model without eroding the distinct economic advantages of either.

A Tale of Two Systems: Deciphering the Economic Models

The central challenge of the Jetro deal is that Sysco and Jetro operate on entirely different economic "engines." Sysco's traditional model is built on Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) and Service Density. It relies on long-term contracts, credit terms, and high-frequency delivery to maximize its ROIC through narrow margins (~4.3% EBIT) spread over massive volume.

In contrast, Jetro Restaurant Depot operates a Cash-and-Carry model characterized by:

High Inventory Turnover: No delivery infrastructure allows for leaner operations.

Zero Credit Risk: Transactions are settled immediately, creating a superior cash conversion cycle.

High Margins: Jetro generated approximately 13% EBITDA margins in 2025, nearly triple Sysco's standalone EBIT margin.

Real Estate Moat: Jetro's value is tied to its 166 convenient, high-traffic urban locations rather than a fleet of trucks.

These are not merely different channels; they are different species of business. Critics argue that the burden of proof lies with Sysco to show that "Project Recipe for Growth" can manage both simultaneously. To mitigate this risk, management has stated that Jetro will operate as a standalone business segment with its original leadership intact. This suggests a strategy of "coordinated autonomy", leveraging Sysco's massive procurement scale to lower Jetro's cost of goods sold (COGS) without forcing Jetro into Sysco's rigid delivery-focused ERP systems.

Story Continues

The Burden of Proof: Why This Combination (Theoretically) Creates Value

To justify a $29 billion price tag and a spike in leverage to 4.5x5.0x EBITDA, Sysco must prove that the combined entity is more than the sum of its parts. The value-creation thesis rests on three specific pillars of synergy:

Procurement Hegemony: Sysco is 1.3x larger in purchasing scale than its closest peers. By folding Jetro's $16 billion in annual spend into its strategic sourcing engine, Sysco expects to realize $250 million in annualized net cost synergies within three years. This is not just "back-office" savings; it is the structural lowering of COGS for Jetro's "value-tier" customers.

The "Fill-In" Loop: Approximately 60% of independent restaurants currently "fill-in" their inventory by visiting a cash-and-carry store between their weekly Sysco deliveries. By owning both channels, Sysco can use Jetro locations as "micro-fulfillment" hubs for its own delivery business, potentially solving the expensive "last-mile" problem in dense urban centers where large broadline trucks struggle to navigate.

Specialty Cross-Pollination: Sysco's $10 billion specialty platform (premium proteins and produce) can be introduced to Jetro's shelves. Jetro historically focused on bulk, shelf-stable, or standard-grade items. Integrating Sysco's high-margin specialty items into Jetro's warehouses provides an immediate "upsell" opportunity to the 725,000 independent operators who shop at Jetro.

The FCF Engine: Financing the $29 Billion Bet

The Jetro deal is, at its core, a "Free Cash Flow (FCF) acquisition." While the $21.6 billion cash component was funded by a massive $22 billion bridge loan, pushing net debt to $33 billion, the underlying math is driven by Jetro's superior cash generation.

In 2025, Jetro produced $1.9 billion in FCF on $2.1 billion of EBITDA, a staggering 90%+ conversion rate. By comparison, Sysco's capital-intensive delivery model (fleet, fuel, high maintenance) has a lower conversion profile. The pro-forma entity is expected to generate $5.5 billion in annual FCF, a 55% increase over Sysco's standalone figures. This $5.5 billion is the "lifeblood" of the thesis; it is the capital required to reduce net leverage by 1.0x within the first 24 months, service the higher interest expense on $33 billion of debt without touching the dividend, and fund the expansion of 125+ new Jetro warehouses over the next two decades.

Execution in a Softening Macro Context (Q4 2025 Q2 2026)

Before the Jetro announcement, Sysco demonstrated relative execution strength during a period of macroeconomic softening. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Sysco reported sales of $20.8 billion (+3.0%) and adjusted EPS of $0.99 (+6.5%). These results were particularly notable because they occurred while restaurant industry traffic (per Black Box) declined more than 200 basis points.

Sysco's ability to gain market share in a down-cycle is attributed to its AI 360 CRM tool, which now sees 95% weekly adoption among sales teams. This tool powers the "Swap and Save" initiative, which helps restaurants mitigate food-cost inflation by switching to higher-margin Sysco-branded products, which now account for 35.6% of broadline cases. This relative execution is the "floor" of the investment thesis: Sysco's core business is healthy enough to support the "weight" of the Jetro integration.

Valuation Analysis

Evaluating Sysco's valuation as of April 2026 requires a comparison between its current multiples, its historical averages, and the valuation of its primary peers. Sysco's forward P/E ratio is currently approximately 16.19. This represents a significant discount compared to its five-year average forward P/E ratio, which has historically stood at 29.14. The current multiple is also 34% lower than its ten-year mean historical P/E ratio of 29.87. This compression reflects the market's "leverage discount" following the Jetro announcement, as investors weigh the risks of high debt against the benefits of the acquisition.

With Sysco's stock trading around $73.00 to $75.00 and TTM EPS at $3.71, the TTM P/E ratio is approximately 19.63 to 20.2. When compared to the broader Consumer Defensive sector and the Retail-Defensive industry, Sysco appears undervalued, as the industry average P/E ratio stands at 38.18. This suggests that while the market is punishing Sysco for its debt load, the core earnings power of the business is being valued more conservatively than its peers.Sysco Corporation: Dominating the Plate

A peer comparison highlights Sysco's relative value. Primary rival US Foods (USFD) trades at a TTM P/E of 31.04, and Performance Food Group (PFGC) trades at 40.38. While Sysco's net margin of 2.2% is higher than both US Foods (1.7%) and PFGC (0.6%), the market is currently assigning a higher multiple to the smaller rivals, potentially due to their simpler capital structures and higher recent stock price momentum. However, Sysco's 3.0% dividend yield and Dividend King status provide a significant advantage for income-focused investors that neither USFD nor PFGC currently offers (PFGC does not pay a dividend).

Guru Activity: The Moves of Institutional Titans

As of late 2025 and early 2026, Sysco maintains high institutional ownership at 87.91%, suggesting it is a staple in many large-scale defensive portfolios. However, recent filings show some tactical shifts among high-profile investors.

Nelson Peltz (Trades, Portfolio) of Trian Fund Management, a founding partner and long-time major holder of Sysco, reduced his firm's position in the stock during the third quarter of 2025.36 Trian sold 1,615,617 shares, trimming the position by 18.37%. Despite this reduction, Sysco remained the firm's fourth-largest holding with a portfolio weight of 13.36%.36 This move may reflect a desire to lock in gains or rebalance a highly concentrated portfolio, as Trian also trimmed its top holding in Ferguson during the same period. Peltz's involvement with Sysco has historically been focused on driving operational efficiencies and margin expansion, goals that remain central to the "Recipe for Growth" strategy.

Other notable data includes low insider ownership at 1.39%, with GuruFocus identifying "insider selling activity" as a cautionary warning sign for prospective investors. The "Moderate Buy" consensus from Wall Street analysts also reflects a divided sentiment following the Jetro announcement, with some brokers like Piper Sandler cutting price targets (to $77) while others like JPMorgan upped targets (to $87). This divergence in guru and analyst opinion underscores the "bet-the-farm" nature of the current strategic pivot, as institutional investors weigh the long-term margin potential of a multi-channel leader against the immediate risks of high leverage and dilution.

Conclusion

The investment thesis for Sysco Corporation has pivoted from a stable broadline distribution story into a high-stakes "beta test" of multi-channel industrial logic. By deploying $29.1 billion to acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot, management has essentially bet its 52-year legacy of capital-allocation discipline on the premise that its $81 billion procurement engine can structurally enhance a high-margin, cash-and-carry model without the friction of corporate over-integration. The current 44% discount in the forward P/E ratio relative to its five-year average (16.19 vs 29.14) indicates that the market currently views the $21 billion in new debt as a balance sheet liability rather than a strategic asset.

However, the "burden of proof" for a valuation re-rating rests entirely on the ability of the pro-forma entity to sustain Jetro's staggering 90%+ FCF conversion rate, which is projected to swell combined annual free cash flow to $5.5 billion, a 55% increase that provides the necessary ammunition for rapid de-leveraging and dividend protection. While the cultural friction between Sysco's process-driven logistics and Jetro's lean, entrepreneurial model remains a monumental execution hurdle, the core business's recent ability to outpace industry-wide traffic declines by 140 basis points suggests a level of relative execution that provides a sturdy floor for this transition. For the patient investor, Sysco no longer represents a defensive bond-proxy, but rather an asymmetric entry point into a dominant, multi-channel powerhouse with a pro-forma EBITDA margin of 6.7%, offering a structural profit advantage that primary peers US Foods and Performance Food Group cannot currently replicate.

title: Sysco Corp (SYY) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Strong Revenue Growth and Strategic ...
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Total Revenue: Nearly $21 billion, a growth rate of 4.7% year-over-year. Adjusted Earnings Per Share (EPS): $0.94, in line with expectations. Local Volume Growth (US Business): 3.3%, a 210 basis point improvement versus the prior quarter. Gross Profit: Up 6.5% year-over-year. Gross Margin Expansion: 31 basis points to 18.6%. International Segment Local Case Growth: 3.8% in the quarter. Adjusted Operating Income: $768 million for the quarter. Free Cash Flow: Grew 19% year-to-date. Inflation Rates: Approximately 2.8% for the enterprise, 0.5% for USPL. Adjusted Operating Expenses: $3 billion for the quarter, 14.8% of sales. Net Debt Leverage Ratio: 2.80 times. FY26 Adjusted EPS Guidance: Expected at the high end of $4.50 to $4.60. Dividend Growth: Approximately 6% increase year-over-year.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with SYY. Is SYY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: April 28, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) reported strong results in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, with a 4.7% revenue growth to nearly $21 billion. The company achieved a 3.3% local volume growth in its US business, marking the strongest quarter of local volume growth in three years. Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) delivered an adjusted earnings per share of $0.94, in line with expectations, despite a $63 million headwind from lower incentive compensation in the prior year. The acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot is expected to enhance Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY)'s growth, profitability, and shareholder value, with plans to open 125 new locations over time. Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) is confident in delivering at least 2.5% local volume growth in the fourth quarter, indicating continued momentum in its core business.

Negative Points

Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) faces challenges from declining foot traffic to restaurants, which has affected its national chain restaurant customers. The acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot has raised investor concerns about integration risks and the $29.1 billion purchase price. Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) has suspended its share repurchase program to preserve cash for the acquisition, impacting potential shareholder returns. The company is dealing with a $100 million headwind from lapping lower incentive compensation in fiscal 2025, affecting adjusted EPS growth. Sysco Corp (NYSE:SYY) has seen a decline in private label sales as a percentage of broadline in US Foods year-over-year, indicating potential challenges in brand penetration.

Story Continues

Q & A Highlights

Q: Kevin, the first question is just on the Restaurant Depot acquisition. It seems like investors appear cautious, contrary to your enthusiasm. Can you share what investor feedback you've gotten in terms of the primary drivers of that concern? A: What we've heard from investors are two things. First, Restaurant Depot was an unknown entity as it was privately held, and its size and profitability were not visible to investors. Second, the purchase price of $29.1 billion surprised some. However, as investors learn more about Restaurant Depot, they become more excited. We plan to invite investors to tour with us and meet some of the key leaders from Restaurant Depot. We believe that the more investors learn about Restaurant Depot, the more they'll appreciate the acquisition.

Q: The follow-up is just on the restaurant trends. The US local garnering all the attention, 3.3%, a very nice acceleration on a one-year basis. How do you assess your underlying two-year or one-year trend, and do you feel good about the outlook considering the more cautious industry perspective? A: Both one-year and two-year trends matter. From a traffic perspective, Q2 into Q3 improved by 90 basis points, and Sysco's performance improved by 210 basis points, showing our progress is from actions within our control. We reiterated 2.5% volume growth for Q4, which is an acceleration on a two-year stack basis of 120 basis points. We don't need the macro to improve for Sysco to deliver that outcome, thanks to improvements in sales colleague retention and productivity.

Q: Can you touch on the composition of net new account wins? Have the losses, the account losses, normalized to where they were a couple of years ago? A: We track new, loss, and penetration across all customer types. We saw continued acceleration in new accounts, driven by increased sales consultant headcount. We are seeing improvement in loss, but there's still room for improvement. Our strongest penetration performance in Q3 in a long time is due to selling effectiveness, and we are confident in our ability to continue making progress.

Q: Any updates on the cadence of local volumes? How does this lead to the 2.5% local case outlook for fiscal Q4? A: April's performance was in line with our expectations, and we are on track to deliver at least 2.5% local volume growth in Q4, which is an acceleration of 120 basis points on a two-year stack basis. We had consistent results across all geographies, and the usage of AI360 is increasing, which gives us confidence in our volume growth and penetration.

Q: A question about Restaurant Depot and the $250 million in net cost synergies. Is the goal to reinvest some of the costs into lower prices for customers? A: The $250 million net refers to the cost synergies after investing in making Restaurant Depot a public company, such as SOX compliance and cybersecurity. The synergies are mostly merchandising synergies from increased purchasing efficiency. The $250 million is what would drop to the bottom line, and any over-delivery against that target could be shared with customers responsibly.

title: Sysco Corporation Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Sysco Corporation Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers and Operational Context

Delivered 3.3% local volume growth in the U.S., marking the strongest performance in three years despite a 1.9% decline in overall restaurant foot traffic. Performance improvement was driven by internal sales initiatives, specifically increased sales colleague retention and productivity gains from AI360 enablement tools. Gross margin expansion of 31 basis points was fueled by strategic sourcing efforts and sequential improvements in Sysco Brand penetration. International segment achieved its tenth consecutive quarter of double-digit operating income growth, supported by expanded supply chain capacity and sales headcount. National contract business saw 1.4% volume growth, where strength in healthcare and hospitality offset softness in the national restaurant chain segment. Management attributes the local volume beat to 'selling initiatives within direct control' rather than macro improvements, citing a 210 basis point improvement over the prior quarter.

Outlook and Strategic Integration Framework

Reiterated full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS at the high end of the $4.50 to $4.60 range, assuming continued local volume momentum. Expects Q4 local volume growth of at least 2.5%, representing a 120 basis point acceleration on a two-year stack basis. The Restaurant Depot acquisition is projected to close by Q3 fiscal 2027, with plans to open 5 to 6 net new stores annually for the next 25 years. Management committed to reducing net leverage from approximately 4.5x at deal close to 3.5x within the first 24 months post-acquisition. Identified $60 million in run-rate cost savings through organizational efficiency activities beginning in Q4 to offset the suspension of share repurchases.

Non-Recurring Items and Acquisition Dynamics

Q3 results included a $63 million headwind ($0.10 per share) from lapping lower incentive compensation in the prior year. Suspended the remaining $800 million of planned share repurchases for fiscal 2026 to preserve cash for the Restaurant Depot transaction. The Restaurant Depot acquisition includes $250 million in targeted net cost synergies, primarily from combined purchasing power rather than headcount reductions. Management addressed concerns regarding Restaurant Depot's low CapEx (less than 1% of sales), clarifying that the model lacks the expensive delivery fleet required for Sysco's core business.

Investor skepticism regarding the $29.1 billion Restaurant Depot purchase price

Management acknowledged the asset was previously 'unknown' to public markets but highlighted 30 consecutive years of profit growth. Emphasized that the deal is immediately accretive and provides access to a resilient $60 billion to $70 billion cash-and-carry market.

Sustainability of Restaurant Depot's 13% EBITDA margins

The high margin is driven by a 'no-frills' warehouse model where customers perform the labor of picking and transporting goods. Management noted that Restaurant Depot's 100% local customer profile aligns with the margins Sysco sees in its own small-customer segments.

Strategy for private label growth and brand rationalization

Sysco is using 'Swap & Save' AI tools to prompt sales consultants to convert customers to private labels when it saves the customer money. Management plans to leverage Restaurant Depot's value-tier assortment to fill gaps in Sysco's delivery catalog, targeting customers not currently buying in specific categories.
